meta.label: Electric toothbrushes
tradeoffLabels: ADA-reviewed for safety and plaque removal
meta.attribution: The ADA Seal of Acceptance is a voluntary US programme: a manufacturer submits its own test data and the ADA's Council on Scientific Affairs decides whether it shows the product is safe and effective at removing plaque and reducing gingivitis when used as directed. A brush that does not appear in the ADA's product-search tool has not necessarily failed anything; it may simply not have applied, especially if the brand sells mainly outside the US. Where a search turned up no result for a brand, the note says so and gives the date checked, rather than treating the absence as a safety finding. Where the note also cites the US Consumer Product Safety Commission's saferproducts.gov recall database, that is a separate, government-run check of whether that brand name has any recall on file, most relevant to battery and charger hazards; the CPSC's own database shows a 2026 recall of a children's toothbrush kit (not scored on this page) for a lithium coin battery that small children could reach, which is the kind of hazard this check is meant to catch. Price here is the toothbrush handle's own listed price on the date shown, not the ongoing cost of replacement heads, which varies by brand, subscription plan and how often a head is changed, and is not scored here. Two models from the same maker (Oral-B iO against Oral-B Pro 1000, quip's rechargeable against its AAA-battery model) are scored separately because the ADA lists them under separate records and their prices and designs differ. Not medical advice; the ADA's own guidance is that either a manual or a powered brush works when used for two minutes, twice a day, with gentle pressure. Reviewed 2026-08. Suggest changes via Contribute.

criteria.label: ADA Seal record and CPSC recall check
Ease of purchase and replacement heads

products.name: Manual toothbrush (skip going electric)

economical.note: The ADA's own toothbrush page states powered toothbrushes 'can be more expensive than most manual toothbrushes.'

health.note: The ADA's toothbrush page states 'both manual and powered toothbrushes are effective at removing plaque,' with powered brushes offering a practical advantage mainly for people with reduced dexterity, such as some elderly users, people with disabilities, or people wearing braces.

accessibility.note: A manual toothbrush is sold everywhere a toothbrush is sold, with no charger, no app, and no proprietary replacement head to reorder.

products.description: The ADA's own guidance says manual and powered toothbrushes remove plaque equally well when used correctly for two minutes twice a day; a basic manual toothbrush needs no charging, no subscription and no replacement head to order.

products.name: Oral-B iO Series

economical.note: Oral-B's own site prices the iO Series 4 (Matte White) at $99.99.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Oral-B' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Oral-B iO Series', applicant Procter & Gamble Co., states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: Widely sold through major US retail, but the iO line uses its own head design rather than the round heads shared across most other Oral-B lines, and its $99.99 handle price is the second-highest in this roster.

products.description: Procter & Gamble's premium rotating-oscillating-pulsating line, individually named in its own ADA Seal record, with app-based coaching and a price well above most of this roster.

products.name: Oral-B Pro 1000

economical.note: Oral-B's own site prices the Pro 1000 rechargeable toothbrush at $49.99.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Oral-B' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Oral-B Oscillating-Rotating-Pulsating', applicant Procter & Gamble Co., covers the Pro series (which includes Pro 1000) along with the Genius and Smart series, and states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: One of the most widely stocked electric toothbrushes in US grocery, pharmacy and big-box retail, with round replacement heads shared across most Oral-B lines except iO.

products.description: A basic Oral-B rotating-oscillating brush covered by the same ADA Seal record as Oral-B's Pro, Genius and Smart lines, at about half the price of the iO line.

products.name: Philips Sonicare ProtectiveClean 4100

economical.note: Target's listing shows the Philips Sonicare 4100 Plaque Control at $39.99, marked down from a regular price of $49.99.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Sonicare' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Philips Sonicare ProtectiveClean' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed; the 4100 is Philips' entry model in the ProtectiveClean line.

accessibility.note: Widely stocked at major US retailers such as Target and Walmart, with one cleaning mode and a pressure sensor as its main features.

products.description: Philips' entry sonic model, covered by the ADA's record for the Sonicare ProtectiveClean line, with a single cleaning mode and a pressure sensor.

products.name: quip Smart Rechargeable

economical.note: quip's own site lists the Smart Rechargeable Sonic Toothbrush at $55.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'quip Electric Toothbrush - Rechargeable' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed. This is a separate ADA record from quip's battery-powered model.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through quip's own site, built around a recurring replacement-head plan rather than one-off retail purchase.

products.description: quip's rechargeable sonic brush, listed separately from its battery model in the ADA's product search, built around a subscription refill-head plan.

products.name: quip Metal (AAA battery)

economical.note: quip's own site lists the Twilight Metal Sonic Toothbrush, its AAA-battery model, at $35.

health.note: The ADA's product-search record for 'quip Electric Toothbrush - Non-Rechargeable' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed. This is a separate ADA record from quip's rechargeable model.

environment.note: quip's own product page describes this model as running on a single removable AAA battery lasting over 3 months rather than a built-in rechargeable pack, so there is no sealed battery to eventually degrade with the handle, but it does mean buying and disposing of AAA batteries every few months.

accessibility.note: Needs no charging dock or outlet, which can matter for travel or a bathroom without counter space, and a spent AAA battery is easier to replace on the road than finding a proprietary charger.

products.description: quip's other ADA-listed model runs on a single removable AAA battery instead of a built-in rechargeable pack, so there is no charging dock and no dead sealed battery forcing a full replacement, at the cost of buying and disposing of batteries every few months.

products.name: Goby Electric Toothbrush

economical.note: Goby's own site prices the toothbrush at $75 as a one-time purchase, or $60 upfront if the buyer joins the recurring $6 replacement-head plan.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Goby' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Goby Electric Toothbrush' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: Sold mainly direct-to-consumer through Goby's own site and Amazon rather than in physical stores, with a lower price tied to joining a recurring head subscription.

products.description: A direct-to-consumer sonic brush with its own ADA Seal record, sold either as a one-time purchase or at a lower upfront price tied to a recurring head subscription.

products.name: Bitvae Smart Electric Toothbrush

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Bitvae' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Bitvae Smart Electric Toothbrush', applicant Clevo Innovation Inc, states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed.

accessibility.note: Sold mainly through Amazon rather than through a brand site with clear direct pricing; the listing's own title advertises the ADA acceptance.

products.description: A budget sonic brush sold mainly through Amazon marketplace listings rather than a brand storefront, with its own ADA Seal record; a stable brand-site price could not be confirmed, so it is not scored on cost here.

products.name: Laifen Wave

economical.note: Laifen's own site prices the Wave at $69 for the ABS plastic handle, $79 for aluminum alloy, and $99 for stainless steel; replacement heads are $9.99 for a 3-pack.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Laifen' as of the date checked. Separately, the ADA's product-search record for 'Laifen Wave Electric Toothbrush' states the ADA Council on Scientific Affairs found the product safe and effective at removing plaque and helping prevent and reduce gingivitis when used as directed, one of the more recent additions to the ADA's list.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Laifen's own site and Amazon, with an optional companion app; three handle materials at three price points give a buyer more choice than most other brands here.

products.description: A newer sonic-and-oscillating brush with its own ADA Seal record, priced by handle material: plastic, aluminum or steel.

products.name: BURST Sonic Toothbrush

economical.note: Burst's own site prices the Original Sonic Toothbrush at $69.99, with a recurring replacement-head plan at $7 every 12 weeks.

health.note: Burst's own site states of ADA status: 'Stay tuned for ADA acceptance!', meaning the brand itself says it does not currently hold the ADA Seal of Acceptance.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Burst's own site on a subscription model for replacement heads, plus some third-party retail.

products.description: A subscription-model sonic brush; Burst's own site says it is not yet ADA-accepted.

products.name: SURI Pro 2.0

economical.note: SURI's own site prices the Pro 2.0 at $105 for the brush alone or $135 with the UV-C case.

health.note: No result for Suri appeared when searching the ADA's Seal of Acceptance product-search tool on the date checked; absence from a voluntary program is not the same as failing a test, and Suri sells mainly outside the US.

environment.note: SURI's own product page states the brush heads are made from cornstarch and castor oil and are 'fully recyclable' through the brand's free returns program, which is a stronger recycling claim than any other brand scored here.

accessibility.note: Sold direct through SURI's own site only, and at $105 to $135 it is the most expensive brush in this roster, which limits who can consider it.

ethics.note: B Lab's Certified B Corporation directory lists Coral Innovations Ltd, trading as SURI, as a Certified B Corp.

products.description: A UK-made brush from a Certified B Corporation, with brush heads the company recycles for free; it did not turn up in the ADA's product search on the date checked, and it is the most expensive brush in this roster.

products.name: Spotlight Oral Care Sonic Toothbrush

economical.note: Spotlight Oral Care's own EU site prices the Sonic Toothbrush at 69.99 euros.

health.note: The brand's own product page does not claim an ADA Seal of Acceptance or an Oral Health Foundation accreditation; it states only that the brush was 'designed by dentists.'

accessibility.note: Sold direct through Spotlight's own site and through UK retailers such as Superdrug, with up to 70 days of battery life between charges per the brand's own page.

products.description: A UK sonic brush; its own product page makes no claim to an ADA or Oral Health Foundation seal.

products.name: Waterpik Sonic-Fusion 2.0

economical.note: Waterpik's own store lists the Sonic-Fusion 2.0 at $179.99, on sale at $139.99 on the date checked.

health.note: The CPSC's saferproducts.gov recall database returned no recall record for 'Waterpik' as of the date checked. Separately, Waterpik's own product page states the Sonic-Fusion 2.0 'is accepted by the American Dental Association (ADA) for safety and effectiveness,' matching the ADA's own product-search record for 'Waterpik Sonic-Fusion Toothbrush/Flosser.'

accessibility.note: A combined sonic toothbrush and water flosser in one handle, sold through major retailers such as Best Buy and Walmart, but at $139.99 to $179.99 it is the highest price in this roster and is a different, bulkier device than a brush-only model.

products.description: A combined sonic toothbrush and water flosser in one handle, with its own ADA Seal record and the highest price in this roster.
